authority: CEO Round 133: 'Replace common D with common predicted observable. The correct architecture is: solver_internal_state → model_to_observable_mapping → physical_observable Ψ. Then compare Ψ, not the internal state variables.'
supersedes: CROSS_WORLD_OBSERVABLE_CONTRACT.json (Round 132) — that contract normalized internal D variables to [0,1], which is scale normalization, not semantic equivalence.
problem_statement: Round 132's common Phi(t)∈[0,1] was epistemically invalid. FEBio's CDM damage, peridynamics' bond-breakage density, flow's eroded fraction, CalculiX's plastic strain, and SfePy's elastic strain are DIFFERENT physical quantities. Mapping them all to [0,1] and comparing dPhi/dstrain is comparing non-commensurate variables. This is H9_INTERNAL_STATE_NON_EQUIVALENCE.

model_internal_state.definition: A solver-specific variable that the solver uses internally to track failure progression.
model_internal_state.examples: FEBio D_CDM, peridynamics bond_density, flow eroded_fraction, CalculiX plastic_strain, SfePy elastic_strain
model_internal_state.problem: These are NOT the same physical quantity. They have different units, different definitions, different causal relationships to fragmentation. Comparing them directly is meaningless.

physical_observable.definition: A quantity that can be measured by a physical instrument external to the model.
physical_observable.advantage: Physical observables are world-independent. Every solver can predict them from its internal state. Comparing predicted physical observables IS meaningful.

the_mapping.requirement: Every world MUST define a mapping from its internal state to the SAME physical observable. No mapping → no cross-world evidence.

primary_observable.name: Force-curvature sign change
primary_observable.definition: The second derivative of the reaction force with respect to displacement (d²F/dδ²) changes sign from positive to negative before fragmentation onset.
primary_observable.measurement_method: Physical: load cell at ≥100Hz + LVDT at ≥100Hz, synchronized. Computational: extract reaction force at the prescribed-displacement boundary at each timestep.
primary_observable.causal_relationship_to_fragmentation: Force curvature sign change indicates that the specimen's tangent stiffness is decreasing — the structure is losing load-bearing capacity. This is a physical precursor to fracture.
primary_observable.validity_domain: Quasi-static loading. Under dynamic loading, inertial effects may mask the curvature signal.
primary_observable.uncertainty: Measurement noise (force sensor), discretization (computational), timestep resolution.
primary_observable.provenance: PEP-SLOT5-001-a2 frozen protocol (Round 123). This is the FROZEN physical endpoint.

secondary_observable.name: Stiffness degradation rate
secondary_observable.definition: dK/dδ (rate of change of tangent stiffness K = dF/dδ with respect to displacement) decelerates (peaks then declines) before fragmentation.
secondary_observable.measurement_method: Computed from force-displacement curve: K = dF/dδ at each point, then dK/dδ.
secondary_observable.causal_relationship_to_fragmentation: Stiffness degradation is a direct measure of structural damage. Its deceleration indicates approaching loss of integrity.
secondary_observable.uncertainty: Sensitive to numerical differentiation noise. Requires careful smoothing protocol (frozen in PEP-SLOT5-001-a2).

fragmentation_onset.name: Fragmentation onset
fragmentation_onset.definition: The displacement at which visible fragmentation first occurs (physical: camera-confirmed; computational: first element deletion or first bond breakage reaching critical density).
fragmentation_onset.measurement_method: Physical: high-speed camera at ≥500fps, blind review by 2+ observers. Computational: first timestep at which D_CDM ≥ D_critical (FEBio), bond_breakage_density ≥ 0.9 (peridynamics), eroded_fraction ≥ 0.9 (flow), plastic_strain ≥ yield (CalculiX), max_strain ≥ failure_strain (SfePy).
fragmentation_onset.cross_world_note: Fragmentation onset IS world-specific in its detection method, but the PHYSICAL event (visible crack/fragment) is the same. The computational methods are predictions of when this physical event would occur.

lead_time.name: Lead time
lead_time.definition: t_fragmentation - t_Ψ_onset (time between precursor signal and fragmentation).
lead_time.units: seconds (at frozen strain rate 0.01 s⁻¹) or strain (dimensionless)

WORLD_A_FEBIO.mapping_to_force: F = ∫ σ(I-D_CDM) : dε dV — reaction force at boundary integrates the damaged stress tensor. FEBio outputs reaction force directly.
WORLD_A_FEBIO.mapping_to_stiffness: K = dF/dδ computed from FEBio force-displacement output at each timestep.
WORLD_A_FEBIO.provenance: FEBio outputs reaction force in .log file. Already extracted in Round 129-131.
WORLD_A_FEBIO.assumptions: Quasi-static. Damage reduces stress proportionally (Simo CDF). Element deletion does not affect force extraction.

WORLD_B_CUSTOM_PERIDYNAMIC_FORMULATION.mapping_to_force: F = Σ_bonds k_bond × (current_length - original_length) for intact bonds — total bond force at boundary. Currently NOT computed in the custom implementation.
WORLD_B_CUSTOM_PERIDYNAMIC_FORMULATION.mapping_to_stiffness: K = dF/dδ — requires computing F first, then differentiating. Currently NOT computed.
WORLD_B_CUSTOM_PERIDYNAMIC_FORMULATION.next_action: Add force computation to the peridynamics solver: sum bond forces at boundary particles. This is a straightforward code addition.
WORLD_B_CUSTOM_PERIDYNAMIC_FORMULATION.assumptions: Bond forces are linear (prototype microelastic). Boundary particles represent the loading surface.

WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.mapping_to_force: F = flow_pressure × remaining_clot_area — hydrodynamic force on clot. Currently NOT computed.
WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.mapping_to_stiffness: K = dF/dδ — requires force computation. Currently NOT computed.
WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.next_action: Add force computation: F = pressure × area at each timestep. The flow model currently tracks erosion but not force.
WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.assumptions: Uniform pressure. No viscous effects. Simplified hydrodynamics.
WORLD_C_CUSTOM_FLOW_FORMULATION.critical_note: The custom flow model's 'precursor detection' was based on eroded_fraction evolution, NOT on force curvature. The physical observable (force) has NOT been computed. The detected 'precursor' may be an artifact of the erosion model, not a physical force-curvature signal.

WORLD_D_CALCULIX.mapping_to_force: F = Σ_elements σ_plastic : dε dV — CalculiX outputs reaction force in .frd file.
WORLD_D_CALCULIX.mapping_to_stiffness: K = dF/dδ from CalculiX force-displacement output.
WORLD_D_CALCULIX.provenance: CalculiX outputs reaction forces. Already partially extracted in Round 131 (max displacement parsed).
WORLD_D_CALCULIX.assumptions: Small strain plasticity. von Mises yield. J2 flow theory.

WORLD_E_SFEPY.mapping_to_force: F = E × ε × A (Hooke's law, linear elastic) — force at boundary.
WORLD_E_SFEPY.mapping_to_stiffness: K = E × A / L (constant for linear elastic). No stiffness degradation possible.
WORLD_E_SFEPY.provenance: SfePy outputs displacement field. Force computed from constitutive law.
WORLD_E_SFEPY.assumptions: Linear elastic. No damage. No plasticity. Constant stiffness.
WORLD_E_SFEPY.validity_domain: Elastic regime only. Cannot predict failure (no failure model).
WORLD_E_SFEPY.limitation: SfePy's linear elastic model CANNOT produce a stiffness-degradation precursor because stiffness is constant by construction. SfePy can only contribute to the elastic-regime baseline, not to precursor detection.

what_this_changes.old_approach_Round_132: Normalize all D variables to [0,1], compute dPhi/dstrain, compare. INVALID because D variables are non-commensurate.
what_this_changes.new_approach_Round_133: Each world computes the SAME physical observable (force, stiffness) from its internal state. Compare predicted force-curvature and stiffness-degradation across worlds. VALID because force is a physical quantity measured in Newtons, not a solver-internal variable.
what_this_changes.implication_for_C5: The custom World C's 'precursor detection' was based on eroded_fraction, NOT on force curvature. It has NOT computed the physical observable. The 'positive result' is therefore NOT evidence for the C5 precursor hypothesis — it is evidence that the erosion model produces a certain D evolution, which is a different claim entirely.

h9_addition.name: INTERNAL_STATE_NON_EQUIVALENCE
h9_addition.description: The apparent world disagreement is caused by comparing solver-specific internal failure variables (CDM damage, bond density, eroded fraction, plastic strain, elastic strain) rather than a common physical observable. Even perfectly extracted values would not be commensurate because the variables represent different physical constructs.
h9_addition.rationale_for_high_posterior: This is now the HIGHEST-probability explanation because Round 132's cross-world comparison was based on non-equivalent internal variables. The 'discrepancy' may be an artifact of comparing apples to oranges. Until each world computes the same physical observable (force curvature), no cross-world comparison is valid.
h9_addition.discriminating_experiment: C5-CONTRA-E03-V2: compute force-curvature (d²F/dδ²) in ALL 5 worlds. If the discrepancy disappears when comparing force (physical) instead of D (internal), H9 is confirmed and the original discrepancy was an artifact.

experiments.description: Add force computation to each world (some already have it: FEBio, CalculiX). Compute d²F/dδ² in all worlds. Compare force-curvature precursor — NOT internal D.
experiments.status: EXECUTABLE_NOW — requires code addition to custom Worlds B and C; FEBio and CalculiX already output force

experiments.description: Replace custom World C with actual clotFoam. Compute force, not just erosion.

experiments.name: Actual Peridigm cross-form test
experiments.description: Replace custom World B with actual Peridigm. Compute force.

revised_experiment_ranking.next_best_experiment: C5-CONTRA-E03-V2 — compute force curvature in all 5 worlds. This is the HIGHEST acquisition score (0.076) and is executable now. It directly tests H9 (the highest-posterior hypothesis at 0.40).

hard_evidence_rule.enforcement: The machine must automatically reject any claim of external independent confirmation from a custom in-repository formulation. Custom models can show that a different mathematical formulation produces a different result (model-form diversity), but they cannot substitute for external solver evidence.
hard_evidence_rule.implementation: In the G18 evaluator, worlds with classification=INTERNAL_CUSTOM_FORMULATION contribute to FORMULATION_DIVERSITY but NOT to EVIDENCE_SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE. Only worlds with classification=EXTERNAL_SOLVER or EXTERNAL_PACKAGE contribute to EVIDENCE_SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE.
